title: Do classical one-way functions exist?
formal: Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time computable function f on binary strings such that every probabilistic polynomial-time inverter, given (1^n, f(U_n)), succeeds in finding any preimage of f(U_n) with only negligible probability, where U_n is uniform on n-bit strings?
context:
This is unconditional existence. Deriving one-way functions from P≠NP or other assumptions is a separate question.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks for the unconditional existence of the basic computational asymmetry underlying much of modern cryptography.
